claims.Finding: Constructor aligns the supplied region to 16 bytes, reserves a 128-byte prefix, and requires end > aligned base+176. A 177-byte region can be constructed but cannot fit an ordinary minimum 64-byte block. Multiple instances reuse the global AC0FD8 semaphore wrapper without an instance count in this body.
claims.Limitations: Valid caller-provided memory and native helper contracts remain prerequisites. Simulated helper creation failure is not a live Windows failure.

claims.Finding: Allocation rounds payload to 16 bytes and adds 48 bytes: a 32-byte linked header and two 8-byte trailer markers. It prefers the cached predecessor gap, then first-fit from the sentinel; gaps use DWORD arithmetic. Wait result and size overflow are unchecked, including a reproduced UINT64_MAX wrap to a 48-byte block.
claims.Limitations: Executed privately with recorded dependencies. No real retail oversized request or malformed caller is established.

claims.Finding: Locked Free unlinks the block, updates accounting/cursor, fills DWORDs with EFACCAFE and then clears header+8. NULL still waits/releases. Freed addresses can be immediately reused. No owner/trailer validation appears in this body.
claims.Limitations: The free dependency 3A08F0 is recorded by a stub in the probe; its actual traversal is separately analyzed. This semaphore is not a universal Actor lifetime lock.

claims.Finding: This complete body performs the unlink/accounting/poison operation without allocator semaphore calls. Its incoming references are pdata/chained-unwind records; CHAININFO is not evidence of an EH finally handler.
claims.Limitations: No direct retail caller is recorded; isolated invocation establishes body behavior only.

claims.Finding: The capacity getter returns allocator end(+72) minus block-region start(+64), without acquiring a lock. It is independent of used bytes and largest contiguous free gap.
claims.Limitations: A live caller must separately ensure lifetime and a consistent snapshot.

claims.Finding: The used-byte getter returns QWORD+80 without acquiring a lock. Allocation adds rounded payload plus 48-byte overhead and free subtracts the stored DWORD block extent.
claims.Limitations: This is allocator accounting, not raw payload use or system-process memory consumption.

claims.Finding: Reset rebuilds the sentinel and clears used/cached fields without semaphore, per-block free dependency, or poisoning; it allows prior addresses to be reused.
claims.Limitations: No recorded direct code references; actual retail invocation and concurrent validity remain unproved.

claims.Finding: The sixth primary vtable method clears only cached predecessor+88. The following allocation falls back to a sentinel-first search.
claims.Limitations: No allocator lifetime or synchronization guarantee is added.

claims.Finding: The nondeleting destructor resets vtables, destroys and nulls the shared AC0FD8 wrapper when present, and cleans its CThread subobject at this+8. It does not acquire the allocator semaphore or reference-count peer instances.
claims.Limitations: Artificial overlapping allocator instances confirm the local effect; actual unsafe retail overlap is not established.

claims.Finding: The scalar-deleting destructor performs the same shared-wrapper and thread cleanup, additionally calls j_j_free(this) iff flag bit0 is set, and returns this.
claims.Limitations: Free and CloseHandle are recording stubs in the private probe. Destruction does not establish all object owners have stopped.

claims.Finding: The secondary-vtable entry subtracts eight from RCX and tail-jumps to the scalar-deleting destructor, preserving the flag argument.
claims.Limitations: The pdata reference also pointing at this address is a preceding function EndAddress, not a code call.

claims.Finding: Global allocator replacement calls the old AC0FD0 virtual deleting destructor first, then constructs/publishes the supplied region. A too-small new region publishes null after the old instance has already been destroyed.
claims.Limitations: Only pdata references were recorded; no complete live caller/lifetime contract or semantic return value is established.

claims.Finding: Semaphore-wrapper destruction ignores NULL wrappers; otherwise it calls imported CloseHandle on wrapper+8 and j_j_free(wrapper). The PE import identity is independently verified.
claims.Limitations: Wrapper validity is assumed; CloseHandle outcome is unused and kernel/resource behavior is replaced in the probe.

claims.Finding: CThread destruction sets its vtable, closes and nulls nonzero handle fields +24 and +8, and clears DWORD+48 when +8 was nonzero. As Allocator+8 subobject these map to allocator+32,+16,+56.
claims.Limitations: Return-register contents have no demonstrated semantic contract; asynchronous thread completion is not established.
